facts.statement: The genus Eutreptornis was described by Cracraft in 1971.
Fossils of Eutreptornis date to the Late Eocene epoch.
Eutreptornis, meaning "changing bird", is an extinct bird from the Late Eocene of Utah that may belong to the Cariamiformes group.
facts.quote: Eutreptornis ("changing bird")is a genus of extinct possible cariamiforme bird from the Late Eocene of Utah.

facts.statement: Although traditionally classified as a bathornithid, the incomplete fossil record and differences from other members have raised doubts about this affiliation.
facts.quote: It is traditionally considered to be a bathornithid, though a combination of the relative incompleteness of the material alongside some differences from other bathornithids have raised some suspicions about this affiliation.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from the type species Eutreptornis uintae, which is represented by a tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus found in the Uinta Formation of Utah.
facts.quote: Eutreptornis is currently represented by a single type species, E. uintae, in turn represented by a tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus from the Uinta Formation of Utah.

facts.statement: Eutreptornis holds the record for the smallest known bathornithid remains.
facts.quote: It is represented by the smallest bathornithid remains known.

facts.statement: Eutreptornis was certainly a terrestrial predator, likely similar to its living relatives, the seriemas.
facts.quote: It was, however, most certainly a terrestrial predator, perhaps akin to its closest living relatives, the seriemas.

facts.statement: Eutreptornis lived alongside rich mammalian megafauna like Megacerops and other birds, including larger bathornithids and flightless geranoidids.
facts.quote: Eutreptornis co-existed with a rich mammalian megafauna, such as the brontothere Megacerops, as well as other terrestrial birds, including other bathornithid birds such as the larger Bathornis species and the flightless crane-like geranoidids.

facts.statement: Eutreptornis belongs to the family Bathornithidae.
Eutreptornis lived between 45.9 and 39.7 million years ago, during the Lutetian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Bartonian (45.9 to 39.7 million years ago)
